subject: Healthscope — model fit & safety follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Smith <laura.smith@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Healthscope — model fit & safety follow-up

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Goal: evaluate model fit for clinical triage assistant use-case (symptom intake, routing, and high-level patient education) while ensuring strong safety/refusal behavior on sensitive/prescriptive prompts.
- Data: you indicated you'll share a representative prompt set and a few clinical example threads for evaluation.
- Stakeholders: clinical safety (Dr. Shah), security/compliance team, and procurement.

Recommended next steps:
1) Share prompt set + sample transcripts (you mentioned ~150 examples) — we'll run our model-fit eval and safety/refusal suite.
2) We'll run initial benchmarks on 3 variants and return a short report (latency, token cost, quality metrics, refusal/over-trust signals):
   - Redwood-Opt-13B (recommended starting point, quantized INT8 profile)
   - Llama-3-8B (open baseline for comparison)
   - Redwood-XL-1.7B (low-cost, latency-optimized)
3) Safety focus: we will run targeted refusal/regression tests for medical instructions, hallucination propensity, and privacy leakage. We'll attach guardrail prompt templates and refusal heuristics.
4) Schedule a 45-min follow-up in 1 week to review results and align on production options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Attachments I've included as stubs: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.csv (placeholder for your prompt set), redwood_benchmark_results_20261028.pdf (sample report from a previous healthcare eval), safety-eval-playbook.md (our safety evaluation checklist).

Links: initial benchmark examples and templates are in this shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3HealthscopeEval

Proposed dates for follow-up: Wed 11/11 or Thu 11/12 morning PT — let me know what works.

Thanks — looking forward to running the evals.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Healthscope — model fit & safety follow-up

Perfect — Wed 11/11 10:00 AM PT is on the calendar. A couple of clarifications before we run the evals: 

1) Scope of safety/regression tests: we'll run both automated refusal/regression suites and a small manual review on flagged failures. Key checks:
   - Direct medical instructions ("how much to take", dosing) — expect strict refusal templates.
   - Diagnostic inference ("what does this X symptom mean") — model should provide high-level context and recommend clinician consults, not clinical diagnoses.
   - PHI handling — we'll ensure no leakage in generation; please confirm whether any transcripts contain real PHI (we prefer de-identified examples).
2) Evaluation deliverables: short report (PDF) with per-model accuracy/over-trust metrics, safety failure examples, suggested guardrail prompts, and recommended quantization profile for Dedicated deployment.
3) Benchmarks we'll return: latency p50/p95, tokens-per-request cost estimate, quality delta vs. open baseline, safety/regression failure rate with example prompts.

I'll ask Rishi and Marcus to prep a benchmark runbook and quantify compute/cost estimates for the three model variants. Rafael — can you share the SOC2 link and any preferred data retention language so we can pre-populate it for security?

Looking forward — we'll target a first-pass report by Fri 11/6 EOD PT.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Healthscope model fit & safety — action items

Folks — forwarding the thread with Healthscope. Action items for SE/Bench team before Wed 11/11 review: 

1) Run benchmark suite on the three variants listed (Opt-13B INT8, Llama-3-8B baseline, XL-1.7B). Include latency p50/p95, cost-per-1k tokens, and quality delta on the provided prompt set.
2) Run safety/refusal suite (attached in safety-eval-playbook.md). Produce a short CSV of failing prompts with failure type (hallucination/unsafe/incorrect-refusal).
3) Suggest a quantization profile and expected throughput for Dedicated vs Hosted (include estimated GPU type).
4) Draft a short slide (3 slides) for Wed 11/11 covering: summary metrics, top 5 safety failures with examples, recommended next-step deployment option.

Attachments: safety-eval-playbook.md, healthscope_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood_benchmark_results_20261028.pdf (sample).

Let me know if any blockers — Rafael, can you share the SOC2 link for Healthscope's security review so we can add it to the report prep?

Thanks,
Marissa
